_source: Scirè, Ghonim & Navigli, FENICE: Factuality Evaluation of summarization based on Natural language Inference and Claim Extraction, Findings of ACL 2024, https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-acl.841/. Label definition quoted from Section 4.4 'Human evaluation' (p. 14156): 'we considered a summary factual if its content was explicitly stated or implied by the source document; otherwise, it was labeled as non factual.' Claim definition quoted from Appendix A, Figure 2 (p. 14161): a claim is an 'elementary information unit in a sentence, which no longer needs to be further split.' FENICE scores each claim by its best alignment with the source (Section 3, Eq. 2: max over source passages) and a summary by the mean of its claim scores; Jev replaces that NLI claim/source verification. Claims come from the paper's released T5 claim extractor (Babelscape/t5-base-summarization-claim-extractor). Zero-shot; no dataset rows appear in this prompt.

_template_fields.{claim}: one claim extracted from the summary under evaluation
_template_fields.{scope}: 'whole' for a one-request document; otherwise 'version' and/or 'part' (in that order, joined by a space) filled with {version}/{versions} and {part}/{parts}

scope.whole: The state holds the full text of the source document ("source_text").
scope.part: The source document is too long for one request, so the state holds one contiguous part of it ("source_text"; part {part} of {parts}). The claim counts as supported by the source document if any part supports it; judge it against the part you are given.
scope.version: The source document exists in {versions} English translations and the summary was written from one of them; the state holds version {version} of {versions} ("source_text"). Judge the claim against the version you are given.

criteria.true: Yes: the content of the claim is explicitly stated or implied by the source text.
criteria.false: No: the content of the claim is not stated or implied by the source text (it is absent from it or contradicts it).
